scenario: [IRET.11.3.2]: refraction is the flag on the activation, and a match blocked and released by a negated condition within ONE pump is re-created and fires again. `formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla`'s `same_pump_rel` stream, as DS source. `seen` fires on A (no B yet); `block` emits B `logical`, justified by its own match (A with no C), which blocks `seen`'s token; `stop` emits C, which ends `block`'s match, so truth maintenance retracts B ([IRET.12]) and `seen`'s token is released; `seen` fires a second time in the same pump. `stop` reads A, not B, so the rule graph has no cycle through the `no`. The per-pump reading fires `seen` once ([seen, block, stop]); the flag reading fires it twice. Source order fixes the sequence ([LDET.5.4]): seen, block, stop, seen. Path: libds's terminal refraction table, whose entry goes stale because B's assert and its truth-maintenance retract each advance the generation (rete/wm_rete.c) -- rete/engine.h's comment on cycle_generation; Mercury's ds.agenda.forget, which drops the identity the block removed.
rules_ds:
schema A scope logical:
    k: Int key

schema B scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema C scope logical:
    v: Int key

rule seen:
    A
    no B
->
    log info "seen"

rule block:
    A a
    no C
->
    emit B logical v: a.k

rule stop:
    A a
->
    emit C logical v: a.k
